result:
Round 311 (PERF-4e) is implemented and nothing hit a STOP. It now waits for C's browser checks; I didn't run any browser rows myself, and nothing is committed.

**What changed** (only the 3 granted files plus the new doc):
- **`workers/r2-proxy.js` and `cloudflare/r2-worker.js`:** I replaced only the helper block, from `const PUBLIC_EXPOSE_HEADERS` to the end, and it is byte-identical to B's sketch.
  - **Huge Range (GATE310-M1):** a length or suffix too large to be an exact whole number in JavaScript is no longer sent to R2 as written. The request gets a 206 with the whole object instead of a 500.
  - **Re-read checks (GATE310-L3, C-R310-01):** after an If-Range mismatch, the second read now takes its ETag from the second object and answers If-None-Match with a 304. This holds on both code paths.
  - Everything above that line is byte-identical to HEAD in both files, and the diff between the two blocks is empty, so the protected routes are untouched.
- **`workers/r2-proxy.test.mjs`:** this is B's sketch file exactly.
- **New `docs/implementation/2026/quarter-IV/227-perf-r2-worker-range-guard.md`:** line 4 and the 7 template headings are correct.

**Checks I actually ran:**
- **Claims:** equal to B's HEAD output before editing; after editing, the changed values match B's expected ones.
- **Unit tests:** 75 of 75 pass (about 0.27 s); the two vitest files pass 32 of 32 (936 ms).
- **New tests on the HEAD workers:** exactly B's 4 failures (PR16 and PR17, in both copies).
- **Mutants:** all 25 fail the tests, on exactly the same rows as B's list, and the restored code passes 75 of 75.
- **Typecheck and lint:** both pass; lint shows 205 warnings and 1 info, the same as round 310. Biome skips the worker folders, so I ran `node --check` on both workers and the test file instead.
- **Scope:** only the 3 modified files fail the frozen checksum list.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer subagent ran twice and found no Critical, High or Medium issue (8.5/10, then 9/10 on the doc fixes).
- I corrected doc 227 where it overstated the guard. It covers only length and suffix; an unsafe start still reaches R2 but ends as a 416 on an unconditional request. After the second review I made one more wording fix, using the reviewer's own phrasing.
- I left three test-gap Lows for B (A-R311-REVIEW-L2 to L4) because the test file is pinned to B's sketch and the mutant results depend on it:
  - the 304 after a re-read has no assert on its CORS headers;
  - no test covers the branch that deletes the ETag when the second object has none;
  - the new PR15 "every body cancelled" assert only means something in `short` mode.

**For C:** one deleted test line in PR13 contains an `assert`, which C's "no removed assert" check will flag. It was rewritten into the same assert plus a new one, so nothing was weakened.

**Still open:**
- Browser rows for C: WK-GUARD-PROXY, WK-GUARD-ALT, WK-OPS-REGRESSION, WK-HEAD-CONTROL and G311-AUTH.
- Checks against the deployed worker and real R2 can't run here.
- That R2 rejects these oversized values at all is still an assumption.
- The full suite, build and verify are left to the gate.

**For B (not acted on):** the reviewer's architecture note says to keep the two identical worker copies for now. Merging them is the existing R2-WORKER-TWO-COPIES item and waits for SABA-Q-WORKER-DEPLOYED.

The full report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-311.md`, with logs in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-311/`.
